summary: PARTIAL is right. The expensive time-to-listen parts are done: bin.mjs is a 3.2 KB shim, the Codex schema, effect-acp, noble, React/zustand, native computer use and the GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure clients are behind import(), and a guard test locks the source graph. The auditor's remaining list misses three things. (1) The biggest remaining item: the whole Hub/E2EE graph (HubConnectorLive 210 KB plus HubIdentityRuntime 483 KB with noble) still loads and evaluates on every boot, right after serve, even when hubConnector.enabled is false (the default). The finding's 'load only when enabled' was not implemented, so the RSS saving it named as unconditional for non-Hub nodes never happens. (2) The eager Forgejo API stack (about 115 KiB) is missing from the remaining list. (3) The device fix the auditor proposed (import() inside the layer) would save nothing, because DeviceServiceLive builds localDeviceHost during layer construction on darwin, linux and win32 alike. The tail on the listen path is about 0.6 MiB, not 0.4-0.5. Also, the guard's built-bundle checks never run in CI.
correction:
1. Hub: the auditor said HubConnectorLive and HubIdentityRuntime are import()ed after the router serves, which is true, and treated hub/E2EE as done. But httpServingLayer calls hubConnector.start unconditionally (server.ts:719-726). HubConnectorLive statically imports HubIdentityRuntime (HubConnectorLive.ts:22-26) and the NodeE2ee* modules. So a hub-disabled node (config.ts:72-73 default) still compiles and evaluates about 690 KB of hub/E2EE/noble code on every boot. The finding asked for this code to load only when hubConnector.enabled.
2. Forgejo: ForgejoApi, ForgejoPullRequestPageApi, forgejoDiffLines and forgejoPullRequests* (about 115 KiB in cliMain) stay eager through server.ts:79, ws.ts:13 and SourceControlProviderRegistry.ts:13. Only ForgejoSourceControlProvider is lazy. The auditor listed Forgejo in the summary but left it out of remaining.
3. Device: the sketch 'import() localDeviceHost inside Layer.unwrap' would not help. makeDeviceServiceLayer calls localDeviceHost(platform) while building the layer (DeviceService.ts:58-60), and every supported platform builds it, so the chunk would still load at boot. The local host has to be built on first device operation instead.
4. Wrong line: AgentControlExternalMcpServerLive is server.ts:168 (used at :622), not server.ts:122 (that is AdvertisedEndpointRegistryLive).
5. Tail sizes in the serve closure (bundle region bytes): device 157 KiB, htmlRender 103 KiB (including shared/htmlRender and htmlRenderTools), Atlassian 66 KiB, ExternalMcp 54 KiB, cli.ts plus cliSetup 140 KiB, Forgejo about 115 KiB. That is about 0.6 MiB.

evidence.note: The entry shim only import()s cliMain. dist/bin.mjs is 3,226 bytes. The static closure of dist/cliMain-*.mjs is 6,611,615 bytes in 49 chunks (dist built 21:45, after HEAD at 21:40). Region attribution of that closure finds only effect-codex-app-server/src/errors.ts (3.4 KiB), with no effect-acp, @noble, react or zustand.

Lazy import of effect-codex-app-server/client. SessionImport.ts:28 and CodexMcpService.ts:30-32 are now `import type`. CodexResetCredits loads through providerRpc.ts:44-49 (along with AcpRegistrySupport).

All drivers load through import() inside create. The CodexDriver chunk statically imports the 978 KB client chunk, so the Codex schema still loads soon after serve when Codex is configured. As the original verifier said, this moves the cost off time-to-listen but does not avoid it.
computerBetaTools (502 KB) loads only when config.computerUseBridge.native is set. About 31 KiB of computer guidance/lifecycle stays eager by design.
httpServingLayer calls `yield* hubConnector.start` with no check of config.hubConnector.enabled. HubConnectorDeferred.ts:85-88 then import()s HubConnectorLive.

Static import of makeHubIdentityRuntime from HubIdentityRuntime.ts. In dist, HubConnectorLive-*.mjs (210,405 B) statically imports HubIdentityRuntime-*.mjs (483,246 B, which holds @noble/curves, ciphers, hashes, relayE2ee* and all of hubIdentity). Lines 365 and 384 skip the process lock and custody when disabled, but the module graph is already evaluated by then.
start() returns at once when config.enabled is false. A disabled connector does no work, so building it at boot only costs module compile, eval and heap.

Desktop probes hub reachability only when backendHubLaunch.enabled. The only consumers of HubConnectorReady are the hubConnector HTTP routes (http.ts, localIntroductionHttp.ts, desktopNativeNodeClaimHttp.ts, desktopHubReachabilityHttp.ts), so on-demand construction is viable.

ForgejoApi is a static import (also server.ts:79 and ws.ts:13), deliberately eager for synchronous remote-URL detection (comment at :745-747). It pulls ForgejoPullRequestPageApi (35 KB), ForgejoApi (31 KB), forgejoDiffLines (25 KB) and forgejoPullRequests* (about 25 KB) into cliMain.

Static import of localDeviceHost. Lines 58-60 call localDeviceHost(platform) during layer build, and `supported` is true on darwin, linux and win32. dist/localDeviceHost-*.mjs (143,052 B, with the iOS and Android backends, helperClient and DeviceManager) is statically imported by cliMain.

HtmlRenderLive is a static import (used at :616), and headlessChrome and PreviewBrowser sit in cliMain. Atlassian services are imported at :140-141 and layered at :493-494. AgentControlExternalMcpServerLive is imported at :168 and used at :622. makeExternalMcpTools is built at boot even when the listener stays off (AgentControlExternalMcpServer.ts:44).

cliSetup/nodeSetup and setupFlow (lines 87-108) and every admin command handler (pairing, session, hub, e2ee, project and service, lines 1548-3565) are static. Only remote/threads (:3588) and cliAccountLink (:1867) are lazy.

The built-bundle block is describe.skipIf(!hasCurrentBuild), and hasCurrentBuild only checks that bin.mjs contains 'enableCompileCache'. In CI the test job runs `bun run test` (.github/workflows/_validation.yml:156), and turbo.json's test task depends only on ^build, never on apps/server's own build. So the 7,000,000-byte budget and region checks never run in CI. Locally a stale dist can pass or fail them.

remaining:
On every boot after serve (not on the listen path):
- The Hub/E2EE graph, about 690 KB of bundle (HubConnectorLive plus HubIdentityRuntime with noble), loads even when hubConnector.enabled is false (server.ts:726, HubConnectorLive.ts:22).

Still in the static serve closure (time-to-listen path), about 0.6 MiB of source:
- device: localDeviceHost chunk 143 KB, built during layer construction (DeviceService.ts:19, :58).
- htmlRender: 103 KiB (server.ts:155).
- Atlassian and Jira: 66 KiB (server.ts:140-141).
- ExternalMcp tools and listener: 54 KiB (server.ts:168, AgentControlExternalMcpServer.ts:44).
- Forgejo API stack: about 115 KiB (SourceControlProviderRegistry.ts:13, server.ts:79, ws.ts:13).
- CLI admin handlers and setupFlow: about 140 KiB (cli.ts:87-108, 1548-3565).

Guard gap: the bundle budget and region checks never run in CI (serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts:200).
fixDefects:
No functional bugs in the implemented lazy boundaries. Gaps in the guard:
- The built-bundle assertions (size budget under 7,000,000 B, currently 6,611,615 B, plus forbidden regions and no Codex schema marker) are skipped in CI, because the test job never builds apps/server (turbo test depends only on ^build). They only run when a developer happens to have a dist.
- hasCurrentBuild only greps bin.mjs for 'enableCompileCache', so a stale dist can produce misleading passes or failures.
- The guard does not cover the hub-disabled post-serve load, the device backends, htmlRender, Atlassian, ExternalMcp or Forgejo.
implementationSketch:
1. Hub on demand (largest remaining, S).
   - In HubConnectorDeferred.makeDeferredHubConnectorLive, make HubConnectorReady.await run `start` first. `start` is already idempotent.
   - In server.ts httpServingLayer (~:726), call hubConnector.start only when config.hubConnector?.enabled is true.
   - A disabled node then never import()s HubConnectorLive or HubIdentityRuntime unless a Hub route is hit (Settings > Node security, `leave`, and so on).
   - Why this is behaviour-preserving: a disabled connector takes no process lock (HubConnectorLive.ts:365), opens no custody (:384), HubConnector.start returns early (HubConnector.ts:460), and desktop probes only when the hub is enabled (desktop main.ts:1396).
   - Tests: a HubConnectorDeferred unit test where the load spy is not called until `await` when start was never invoked; a server-layer test that a disabled config never calls the loader.
   - Do not try to just lazy-import HubIdentityRuntime inside HubConnectorLive: NodeE2ee* would still pull noble statically.
2. Device (M).
   - In DeviceService.ts, replace the eager localDeviceHost(platform) with a lazy DeviceHostBackend: a ForwardingDeviceBackend-style wrapper whose first operation does `await import('../localDeviceHost.ts')` and caches the result. Keep the same host id 'local', and keep a single Android adapter instance after first load.
   - Run reclaimOrphanedBoots only when the boot-ownership file has entries, so a clean boot never loads the backends.
   - Keep SshDeviceBackend, deviceFrameRoute and the contracts eager.
   - Check that rolldown moves DeviceManager out of the localDeviceHost chunk (it is now exported from it) into a chunk that cliMain may import statically.
3. htmlRender and Atlassian (M).
   - Add a small HtmlRender facade layer whose methods import('./HtmlRenderLive.ts') (headlessChrome, PreviewBrowser) on first call. htmlRenderTools only needs the service tag.
   - Same pattern for JiraWorkItemService and AtlassianConnectionService. Keep the persistence repositories and migration 036 eager, since migrations must run at boot.
4. ExternalMcp (S).
   - In AgentControlExternalMcpServer.ts, move makeExternalMcpTools and the makeAgentControlExternalListener import into `start` through import(). start only runs when topology.current().available.
5. Forgejo (M).
   - Split ForgejoApi into an eager ForgejoHosts service (configured hosts plus detectProviderFromRemoteUrl, which the synchronous detection needs) and a lazily loaded request client (ForgejoApi, PullRequestPageApi, diff lines), using the existing lazyClient/loadModule pattern in SourceControlProviderRegistry.layer.
   - Update ws.ts:13 and server.ts:79 to depend on the light service.
6. CLI (M).
   - Keep Command/Flag definitions in cli.ts (needed for parsing and --help).
   - Move the handler bodies of pairing, session, hub, e2ee, project and service commands, plus setupFlow, into cliCommands/*.ts, loaded through Effect.promise(() => import(...)) in each withHandler, the same way loadCliRemote works.
7. Guard (S).
   - Run the built-bundle block in CI: add a step to the Build job in _validation.yml after the build (line ~204), e.g. `bun run --cwd apps/server test src/serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts`, with an env flag that turns the skipIf into a hard failure when dist is missing or older than src.
   - Add forbidden-region assertions for src/device/IosSimulatorBackend.ts, src/htmlRender/headlessChrome.ts, src/atlassian/JiraWorkItemService.ts, src/agentControl/ExternalMcp/tools.ts and src/sourceControl/ForgejoPullRequestPageApi.ts in the serve closure, once each is lazy.
decisionReason: These are module-loading boundary changes only. The hub item changes when a disabled connector is built (on the first Hub route instead of after serve). In disabled mode no process lock, key custody or E2EE session is created, so E2EE and auth semantics do not change. If an implementer instead writes a slim disabled-mode HubConnectorService, that touches the E2EE operator and identity surface and should get the identity owner's review.
